welcomeIntro.title: Severe Storm Nowcasting Made Simple
welcomeIntro.message: STORMTRACE predicts thunderstorms and lightning before they happen, using AI trained on radar, satellite, and weather data. Red areas on the map mean a storm is likely soon — use this to know when to take shelter, delay travel, or check on outdoor plans.

walkthrough.step1Desc: StormTrace is an AI-powered convective storm nowcaster that predicts where thunderstorms, heavy rain, and lightning will happen in the next 15 to 120 minutes.
walkthrough.step1Tip: Designed for rapid decision-support during severe convective weather.
walkthrough.step2Desc: Use the top-left buttons to switch between Thunderstorm Risk, Radar Rain Intensity, Satellite Cloud Tops, and Lightning Strikes across the map.
walkthrough.step2Tip: The colormap shows risk levels: blue/green for low, yellow/orange for moderate, and red for severe.
walkthrough.step3Title: 2. Look Ahead into the Future (Lead Time)
walkthrough.step3Desc: Use the Lead Time selector (top right) to see the storm forecast from +15 minutes up to +2 hours. Watch how storm cells move and evolve over time.
walkthrough.step3Tip: Trajectories with yellow dashed arrows show projected direction and speed.
walkthrough.step4Desc: Click on any storm cell on the map or select it in the right sidebar to see its peak rain rate (dBZ), speed, direction, and estimated arrival time to nearby airports.
walkthrough.step4Tip: Always remember: StormTrace outputs are AI decision-support aids, not official IMD warnings.

about.title: About STORMTRACE
about.subtitle: Project Information & Architecture Dossier
about.whatIsDesc: STORMTRACE is an operational AI nowcasting system designed to forecast severe thunderstorm initiation, intense precipitation, and lightning strikes up to 2 hours in advance. It fuses real-time Doppler weather radar composites, geostationary satellite imagery, ground lightning detection, and numerical weather models to give civil authorities and airports rapid situational awareness.
about.dwr: Doppler Weather Radar (DWR): Multi-station radar reflectivity composites cleaned of ground clutter and beam blockage.
about.satelliteDesc: INSAT-3DR / 3DS Satellite: Thermal infrared (TIR1) and water vapor (WV) cloud-top temperature channels.
about.lightningDesc: Lightning Detection Network: Ground-based total lightning flash rate and peak current density.
about.ncumDesc: NCUM Numerical Weather Prediction: Atmospheric instability sounding parameters (CAPE, vertical wind shear, humidity).
about.advisoryDesc: AI decision-support output — not an official IMD warning. All forecasts, cell trajectories, and risk grids are advisory predictions to assist operational meteorologists and disaster response teams.

globalMonitoring.title: Global Coverage & Telemetry Status
globalMonitoring.subtitle: Real-time status of meteorological radar networks, satellite constellations, and lightning sensor coverage across geographic domains.
globalMonitoring.multiRegionBody: STORMTRACE currently operates full end-to-end radar, lightning, and ConvLSTM nowcast AI models for India and adjacent South Asian corridors. For other global regions, high-resolution satellite infrared and NWP layers are served, while local Doppler radar feeds and regional neural weights are being actively onboarded.
